items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Clark Terry told me, he said he was there and the word went out that Buddy’s arm is not broken...

ctx.x: I know. Those guys, they don’t think of themselves like we do.

Yeah. Exactly. It’s always, and the thing with our band, I feel when those guys like, rest their soul, like Sweets and Clark Terry and Tommy Newsom and they come and said, “boy that band sounds good.” And that’s what makes me go even further in my belief, which is almost total. But they won’t tell you that because they’re your friend. Because they played with the greats. And they’re not going to tell you, and I know they’re not, but they go, “Stanley,” you know, “Sherrie.” See they’re secure. The ones that are…
yeah they’re playing, women, all right. Because they’re threatened. See? When you’re not threatened, you’re secure. There’s got to be room for everybody. See?
